title: Review little and often
description: Five minutes of review today can save an hour of relearning next month. Small, regular reviews are the cheapest study habit there is.

body.heading: Forgetting is fast, review is cheap
paragraphs: New learning fades quickly at first: a lesson from Monday can feel half-gone by Friday. A short review interrupts that fade, and each review makes the memory fade more slowly the next time.
The review does not need to be thorough. Skim your notes, retell the main points aloud, or answer three questions from memory. Ten honest minutes is plenty.

body.heading: Build reviews into the week
paragraphs: Add a review to the end of each study session: five minutes on the previous session before starting the new one. Add a slightly bigger one weekly, flipping through everything once, lightly.
Keep a simple list of topics and dates reviewed. Seeing the chain of small reviews grow is satisfying, and it shows you at a glance what has not been revisited for a while.

takeaway: Spend a few minutes reviewing soon and often, and let each review stretch the memory further.
